question:
The first six rows of Pascal's triangle are shown below, beginning with row zero. Except for the $1$ at each end, row $4$ consists of only even numbers, as does row $2.$ How many of the first $20$ rows have this property? (Don't include row $0$ or row $1$). \begin{tabular}{ccccccccccc}
&&&&&1&&&&&\\
&&&&1&&1&&&&\\
&&&1&&2&&1&&&\\
&&1&&3&&3&&1&&\\
&1&&4&&6&&4&&1&\\
1&&5&&10&&10&&5&&1\\
\end{tabular}

The task is to find how many such rows exist from row 2 up to row 19 (since the first 20 rows would be rows 0 through 19, and we are excluding row 0 and row 1).

That would mean that the binomial coefficients C(n,k) for 1 ≤ k ≤ n-1 are even. So the question reduces to finding n such that all C(n,k) for 1 ≤ k ≤ n-1 are even.

Lucas' theorem states that C(n,k) is odd if and only if the binary representations of k is a subset of the binary representation of n. That is, when you write n and k in binary, each bit of k is less than or equal to the corresponding bit in n. 

Therefore, all C(n,k) for 1 ≤ k ≤ n-1 are even if and only if in the binary representation of n, there is only one 1. That is, n is a power of 2. Because if n is a power of 2, its binary representation is a 1 followed by zeros. Then, any k from 1 to n-1 will have a 1 in at least one position where n has a 0, so by Lucas' theorem, C(n,k) would be even.

Lucas' theorem states that for non-negative integers n and k, and a prime p, if n and k are written in base p as n = n_m p^m + ... + n_0 and k = k_m p^m + ... + k_0, then C(n,k) ≡ product_{i=0 to m} C(n_i, k_i) mod p.

Therefore, if n is a power of 2, say n = 2^m, then its binary representation is a 1 followed by m zeros. Then, for any k from 1 to n-1, the binary representation of k will have a 1 in at least one of the positions where n has a 0. Hence, C(n,k) will be even.
